source.title: RIGA at SemEval-2022 Task 1: Scaling Recurrent Neural Networks for CODWOE Dictionary Modeling
source.authors: Eduards Mukans; Gus Strazds; Guntis Bārzdiņš

record.file_problem: The full paper is present. The text refers to figures, but their numerical values are not included in the extracted text.
record.tranche_reason: The study reports epoch-wise double descent in validation cross-entropy loss, showing a non-monotonic loss trajectory rather than a single steadily falling curve. It does not fit or evaluate power laws.
record.gate_note: The paper reports that validation cross-entropy loss has epoch-wise double descent, but provides no numerical loss values in the text. Accuracy and task-metric results are not rows for the claim versions because they do not measure the loss or power-law behavior those versions name. The width/depth tables report MoverScore and BLEU, not loss; scheduled sampling is described as noisy but is not a result about the claim.
record.test_reason: The paper uses 'scaling laws' as framing but fits no power law and reports no loss values. Its one loss result is epoch-wise double descent: validation loss when GRU definition models are trained far past overfitting on a small, fixed 43k-gloss dataset. That regime is data-bottlenecked multi-epoch training on a task model, not held-out pretraining loss with the other factors unconstrained. So it falls outside V1, and it offers no fitted law for V7 to bend from. The width/depth results are task metrics (MoverScore, BLEU) from task-trained models, not downstream predictability from pretraining scale or loss (V6).
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right, with two corrections. The authors call the width/depth improvement only a tentative confirmation, limited to small models within their compute. Their own tables show non-monotonic steps: 2 layers score below 1, and hidden size 4096 scores below 3072. They also conclude that longer training past the first accuracy spike (epoch 5) improves gloss quality per informal human judgement. Double descent is clear only for the 4-layer GRU.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses recurrent GRUs for dictionary-definition generation from word embeddings, with fixed task data and validation measurements; it does not fit the language-model pretraining power laws or use their original setup.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported epoch-wise double-descent effect depends on model size: it is clear for the 4-layer model, while the 1- and 2-layer models are described as too small for the task and training set.

fits_no_version.finding: Validation cross-entropy and token accuracy show epoch-wise double descent when GRUs are trained past overfitting on fixed small data. The effect is clear only for the 4-layer model; the 1- and 2-layer models are called too small (Sec. 4.3, Fig. 1). No numbers are given.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Epoch-wise double descent of validation loss occurs in recurrent models trained many epochs on small fixed data, and it emerges only above a size threshold.

fits_no_version.finding: Scaling GRU width/depth changes task metrics non-monotonically. In Table 2, 2 layers (MoverScore 0.11312) score below 1 layer (0.11458). In Table 3, hidden size 4096 (0.11071) scores below 3072 (0.11312). In Table 4, 1024→3072 rises 0.07284→0.12454.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Task-trained RNN quality on small data improves only roughly and non-monotonically with width/depth.

record.problems: The relevant cross-entropy result is qualitative, with no numerical values or uncertainty estimates in the text. The experiments use a fixed, relatively small task dataset, and the paper says compute capacity limited the model sizes explored.
record.rows_left_out: Width/depth comparisons in Tables 2–4 report MoverScore and BLEU rather than cross-entropy loss or a power-law fit, so they were not included as rows for these versions. Figure 1 concerns accuracy and Figure 2 concerns task metrics; neither provides a reported numerical cross-entropy result in the extracted text.

record.verdict_notes: The reader linked R1 to V1/V7 as challenges/supports. Both labels are removed: epoch-wise overfitting and double descent in a data-limited task setting is a different construct from pretraining power-law loss scaling, and the paper fits no laws. All figure values are absent from the text.

versions.untested_parts: No power-law fit or exponents are reported; it does not test token-count scaling, several-orders-of-magnitude scaling, or held-out pretraining loss. The loss results concern validation loss during recurrent definition-model training.
No prediction of larger runs from fits to smaller runs.
No fixed-compute parameter/token allocation or compute-optimal split.
No comparison of architecture details at a fixed parameter count using loss.
The paper studies recurrent definition modeling, but does not test whether a power-law form holds in that regime or in another modality.
No downstream-task performance prediction from pretraining loss or scale.
No fitted-exponent comparisons or compute-optimal split; the relevant result is epoch-wise loss curvature in this task and model family.

rows.subject: GRU models (1-, 2-, and 4-layer; aggregate result)
rows.operation_detail: Evaluated validation cross-entropy loss across training epochs while varying model size.
rows.value: Epoch-wise double descent; the effect is more pronounced with increasing model size.
rows.note: Aggregate statement; the paper gives no numerical cross-entropy values in the text. Section 4.3 says the 4-layer model shows clear epoch-wise double descent and that the 1- and 2-layer models are apparently too small for this training set and task complexity. The reported curve is non-monotonic rather than a single falling power law.
rows.check: Epoch-wise double descent on a fixed small task dataset is reported only qualitatively, with no values. It concerns overfitting dynamics in a data-bottlenecked regime, not a power law in N/D/C where the other factors are unconstrained. No exponent is fitted, so V7's 'bending away from a fitted law' cannot be assessed. It should not be linked to V1 or V7.
